data.long_meaning: Goddess of the Moon. The name Mahisha carries the meaning “Mysterious, Enigmatic” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. in_arabic.name: ماهشة
in_arabic.meaning: ماهشة تعني الحصانة أو العصمة من الله
in_arabic.long_meaning: ماهشة هي اسم علم مؤنث في اللغة العربية، مشتق من كلمة 'ماه' التي تعني 'الوقاية' أو 'الحصانة'. يوحي الاسم بالحماية الإلهية والعصمة من الله. في بعض التفاسير، يرتبط الاسم بمعاني الصون والرفعة. وقد وردت هذه المعاني في بعض الآيات القرآنية التي تتحدث عن حماية الله لعباده المؤمنين.

in_urdu.name: مہیشہ
in_urdu.meaning: مہیشہ کا مطلب ہے محفوظ یا اللہ کی طرف سے محفوظ
in_urdu.long_meaning: مہیشہ اردو میں ایک خوبصورت اور معانی سے بھرپور نام ہے۔ اس کا عربی मूल ہے جس کا مطلب ہے 'محفوظ' یا 'اللہ کی طرف سے محفوظ'۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی اسلامی ثقافت میں اہمیت رکھتا ہے، خاص طور پر ہندوستان اور پاکستان میں۔ اس نام کی روحانی اہمیت اس میں جڑی ہوئی ہے کہ یہ اللہ کی حفاظت اور دیکھ بھال کی یاد دلاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: माहिषा
in_hindi.meaning: माहिषा का अर्थ है सुरक्षित या ईश्वर द्वारा संरक्षित
in_hindi.long_meaning: माहिषा एक सुंदर और अर्थपूर्ण नाम है जो भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में प्रचलित है। इसका उद्गम अरबी भाषा से है, जिसका अर्थ है 'सुरक्षित' या 'ईश्वर द्वारा संरक्षित'। यह नाम हिंदू-मुस्लिम सांस्कृतिक संदर्भ में महत्वपूर्ण है और अक्सर माता की सुरक्षा और प्रेम के प्रतीक के रूप में देखा जाता है।

in_pashto.name: مهيشه
in_pashto.meaning: مهيشه د خوندیتوب یا د الله د خوندیتوب معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: مهيشه په پښتو کې یو ښکلی نوم دی چې معنی یې 'خوندیتوب' یا 'د الله د خوندیتوب' څخه عبارت دی. دا نوم د افغانستان او پاکستان د پښتنو ټولنو کې منل شوی دی او د الهي حفاظت او پاملرنې مفهوم منعکس کوي.

in_english.name: Mahisha
in_english.meaning: Mahisha means protected or safeguarded by God
in_english.long_meaning: Mahisha is a beautiful and meaningful name derived from Arabic roots. It means 'protected' or 'safeguarded by God'. The name is associated with divine protection and care. In Islamic tradition, it reflects the concept of being under God's shelter and safeguard. Mahisha is used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing spiritual security and peace.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Mahisha" is believed to have originated in Arabic cultures, specifically in reference to the lunar goddess, Manat or Wadd al-Rasat, who was revered in pre-Islamic Arab society. She was considered the "Goddess of the Moon" and was worshipped for protection, fertility, and sustenance. The worship of such goddesses was thus an important part of pre-Islamic Arabian culture. However, with the advent of Islam, this practice was discouraged, and the emphasis shifted towards the One God, Allah. Nevertheless, the legacy of these lunar goddesses continues to be reflected in Islamic art, literature, and folklore.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Mahisha" holds spiritual significance as it is embraced in various forms within the Islamic tradition. Some Sufis, the mystics of Islam, have devised spiritual exercises inspired by the names of these lunar goddesses, acknowledging their inner resonance as metaphors for divine aspects of God. In their contemplative practices, they may use the name "Mahisha," the "Goddess of the Moon," as a reminder of the cyclical, nurturing, and protective qualities of God. Through this symbolic reference, the spiritual significance of the name "Mahisha" extends beyond the pre-Islamic moon goddess, becoming a powerful reminder of the divine presence and the ongoing assurance of God's protection and sustenance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Mysterious, Enigmatic" symbolizes Goddess of the Moon. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Mahisha serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of mysterious, enigmatic.
